rv.q: This production is a visual feast.
Its greatest triumph lies in its ability to create moments of pure joy—those electrifying instances when the music, movement, and narrative fuse into something greater than the sum of their parts.
Weaving the Kenyan legend of the goddess of music with a modern-day love story, Goddess bursts onto the stage at The Public Theater with an explosion of joy.

Everybody does a fine job, but "Goddess" is not always easy to follow, especially when the plot advances, or is at least explained, in a musical number, since the band tends to drown out the lyrics — and Darrell Grand Moultrie's choreography would distract us from the words, even if we could make them out.
It's impossible to have a bad time at Goddess .
If your suspension of disbelief is well-honed, Goddess is captivating.
In its current form, it still offers an evening of foot-tapping pleasures and showmanship — and a memorable star turn for the celestial body that is Amber Iman.
